description: Shishya AstroCoders is a student-led team participating in the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge in Bangalore. We combine software development, space science, AI/ML, data analysis, and creative problem-solving to develop innovative solutions. We welcome passionate participants interested in coding, scientific research, design, data visualization, and space exploration. We value teamwork, curiosity, commitment, and collaboration. Join us to explore ideas, build solutions, and make an impact!
summary:
AstroVital is an astronaut health monitoring and intelligence platform developed by Shishya AstroCoders for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It addresses the health challenges of human spaceflight by bringing together multiple crew-health domains in one integrated platform.

The prototype includes features for vital signs, AI Health Intelligence, human anatomy, radiation monitoring, mental health, predictive analytics, spacecraft environmental information, medical guidance, health reports, crew profiles, and mission timelines.

AstroVital is designed to help organise and explore astronaut health-related information while connecting it with NASA human-spaceflight research. By combining health information, research resources, and mission context, our goal is to support better understanding of the challenges astronauts face during space missions.

Our vision is to make astronaut health information more connected, accessible, and useful for future human space exploration.
details:
AstroVital — Project Details

What does it do?

AstroVital is an integrated astronaut health monitoring and intelligence platform designed around the health challenges of human spaceflight.

The platform brings together the following capabilities:

  • Mission Overview: Central mission information.
  • Vital Signs: Astronaut vital-sign information.
  • AI Health Intelligence: AI-assisted health information and analysis.
  • Human Anatomy: Interactive exploration of human anatomy.
  • Radiation Monitoring: Radiation-related information and research.
  • Mental Health: Crew mental well-being.
  • Predictive Analytics: Identifying patterns and potential risks.
  • Environmental: Spacecraft environmental information.
  • Medical Guidance: Health-related guidance.
  • Mission Timeline: Mission events and tracking.
  • Health Reports: Organised health reports.
  • Crew Profiles: Individual crew information.
  • Research Library: Scientific research resources.
  • NASA Data & Research: Access to NASA research resources.
  • Mission Progress: Mission-related progress tracking.

How does it address the challenge?

Human spaceflight exposes astronauts to five major hazards: space radiation, isolation and confinement, distance from Earth, gravity fields, and hostile or closed environments.

AstroVital addresses this challenge through an integrated software approach that brings together different astronaut health domains, research resources, and mission information.

Creativity and innovation

The project's differentiating approach is its integration of physical health, mental well-being, radiation research, environmental information, AI-assisted health intelligence, predictive analytics, and mission context within one platform.

Rather than treating these areas as completely separate topics, AstroVital aims to make them accessible through a unified interface.

Intended impact

AstroVital aims to support the organisation, exploration, and analysis of astronaut health-related information. Its longer-term vision is to contribute to better-informed human-spaceflight research and mission-health support.

Technologies used

The project was developed using the programming languages, frameworks, tools, and software used by our team. The exact technology stack and external resources are documented in our project repository and submission references.

Factors considered

Our team considered the five hazards of human spaceflight, scientific relevance, usability, data reliability, mission context, accessibility, and the importance of clearly distinguishing research insights from medical diagnosis.

Current limitations

AstroVital is a student-developed prototype. It is not an officially deployed NASA system or a clinically validated medical device. Its outputs should not be treated as medical diagnoses or a replacement for professional medical assessment.
